title: 🚗 Waymo and delivery robots ditch Uber... and want its customers directly!
body: 🚗 Waymo and delivery robots ditch Uber... and want its customers directly!

A new analysis has revealed that self-driving taxi company 'Waymo' has decided to end its exclusive partnership with 'Uber' in Austin and Atlanta, letting riders request its cars directly from its own app starting in January 2028.

Waymo's co-CEO said the mixed-fleet experience was a 'lottery' for customers, because a rider does not know whether the arriving car is a robot or a human driver. 'Serve Robotics', which operates thousands of sidewalk delivery robots, also announced it will not renew its partnership with 'Uber Eats' when it ends in 2027, and will let small stores use its fleet directly.

'Waymo' now runs more than 500,000 paid trips a week through its app across 11 U.S. regions, while 'Uber' replies that it will keep hosting 'Waymo' cars under non-exclusive agreements, and expand its partnerships with other self-driving car companies.

Simply put: 'Uber' was a bridge introducing people to self-driving cars; and now that these companies have grown, they want to own the relationship with their customers themselves, without a middleman.
Do you prefer requesting a self-driving car from the company's own app, or from an app that gathers all the options?
